messages:
carmen: Heads-up: weird behavior in the Python SDK around async function-calling + structured_output. The async client returns a JSON-encoded string for tool_result that itself contains a JSON string (double-encoded). Example: '"{\"id\": 21, \"meta\": "{\\\"active\\\": true}"}"' — nightmare for typing.

devin: whoa that's nasty. sync client returns the parsed object?

carmen: yes sync is fine. Async path seems to both stream and then mistakenly json.dumps the assembled payload again before deserializing. Minimal repro attached below.

lee: can you paste the repro snippet?

carmen: sure:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key='...')
resp = await client.chat.create(
    model='gpt-xyz',
    messages=[{"role":"user","content":"call get_account(21) and return JSON with nested meta"}],
    tools=[{"name":"get_account","schema":{"id":int,"meta":dict}}],
)
# resp.choices[0].message.tool_result -> '"{\"id\": 21, \"meta\": \"{\\\"active\\\": true}\"}"'  # double-encoded string
```

qa-bot: nightly-py-sdk job -> failed: py/test_tools_async.py::test_double_encoded_tool_result (ticket RDW-610).

devin: OK this explains a bunch of customer reports where mypy/type-checkers blow up because tool_result is not Mapping[str,Any] at runtime. Short-term we should: 1) add a helper parse_tool_result(raw) that attempts one or two json.loads and returns a typed dict, 2) update docs/quickstart to recommend using that helper for async examples, 3) add an integration test that simulates streaming + nested JSON metadata.

lee: long-term fix: patch the async streaming deserializer so it never re-encodes the assembled payload. Also tighten types in stubs: AsyncClient.chat.create should annotate tool_result as Union[Mapping[str,Any], str] and add a mypy test that enforces expected types.

carmen: agree. Also request that the runtime exposes both parsed and raw_tool fields (e.g., message.tool_result_raw) so users can opt into raw stream inspection. That helps debugging for private deployments with strict logging.

docs: we'll edit the function-calling guide to include the parse_tool_result helper and a note in the async quickstart about the temporary workaround. We'll also add a short troubleshooting section about double-encoded outputs.

devin: I've opened RDW-610 and assigned to @lee for the runtime patch. I'll add the helper to the SDK util module and a unit test in test_tools_async.py that asserts parse_tool_result returns correct types for double-encoded inputs.

qa-bot: RDW-610 assigned to lee. CI note: flaky=false.

lee: will add the buffer+assemble+single-deserialize fix and include backwards-compatible behavior: if the assembled string looks like a JSON string literal (leading/trailing quotes) attempt an extra json.loads so we don't break existing customers unexpectedly. Also will add a regression test and update changelog entry.

carmen: thanks folks. I'll paste trace logs and a tiny repro harness into the ticket. Please call out the fix in the 0.9.4 patch release notes so enterprise customers expecting stable SDK behavior can plan.

devin: PR incoming later today for the helper and tests; runtime patch PR will follow.
